definitions.explanation: Something that is intended to last indefinitely or for a very long time, without change or end.

examples.japanese: {恒久|こうきゅう}{平和|へいわ}を{願|ねが}う。
{恒久的|こうきゅうてき}な{対策|たいさく}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
{応急処置|おうきゅうしょち}ではなく、{恒久的|こうきゅうてき}な{制度改革|せいどかいかく}を{行|おこな}わなければ{根本的|こんぽんてき}な{解決|かいけつ}にはならない。
examples.english: Without permanent institutional reform rather than just stopgap measures, there will be no fundamental solution.

notes:
FORMATION: {恒|こう} (constant, always) + {久|きゅう} (long time). Both characters convey permanence.

USAGE: {恒久|こうきゅう} is a formal word commonly used in policy, diplomacy, and institutional contexts. The derived form {恒久的|こうきゅうてき} (permanent, as a na-adjective) is very common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {恒久|こうきゅう}{平和|へいわ}: lasting/permanent peace
- {恒久的|こうきゅうてき}な{対策|たいさく}: permanent measures
- {恒久的|こうきゅうてき}な{制度|せいど}: permanent system
- {恒久|こうきゅう}{施設|しせつ}: permanent facility

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {恒久|こうきゅう}: permanent, perpetual (formal, institutional)
- {永久|えいきゅう}: permanent, eternal (broader usage)
- {永続|えいぞく}: perpetuity, continuation
- {暫定|ざんてい}: provisional, temporary (antonym)
